column2: ENGLISH

The atamans of the stanitsa have come to [Root.GetTitledFirstName]. Their lord is not young any more, they say, and the stanitsa must know which of his sons will lead it when Tor calls him home. The old Ungol way gives three choices. The riders can vote in the circle, the sons can fight it out with sabres, or they can wrestle the stanitsa's bear, as their grandfathers did.
Let the riders vote in the circle.
Sabres. The best fighter leads.
Bring out the bear!

[stanitsa_ungol.GetTitledFirstName] comes to court with a gift of horses and a request. The Ungols have ridden for the crown since before the Gospodars came across the mountains, he says, and still no Ungol sits among the druzhina. He asks to be raised to the druzhina and to take his seat in the Boyar Duma. The Gospodar boyars in the hall are very quiet.
You have earned it. Take your seat.
The Duma is not for horse-herders.

An old woman with a staff of bone and a necklace of teeth has come to the gates, and the guards will not touch her. She is a wise woman of the steppe, one of the hags the Ungols go to for curses, cures and the reading of the future. She says the spirits sent her to [Root.GetTitledFirstName]. She did not say why.
Give her a place by the fire.
Ask her to read the omens for us.
Drive the old witch away.

Priests of Ursun ride into the stanitsa in their bearskins, with a letter from [Root.GetLiege.GetTitledFirstName]. The Father of Bears, Dazh of the hearth and Tor of the storm watch over all of Kislev, they say, and the Ungols have ridden under their banners for long enough. It is time the stanitsa kept their altars too. Many of the riders already do.
We ride for Ursun. We will pray to him too.
The old gods of the north have served us well.

Priests of Ursun come into the Ropsmann woods with a letter from [Root.GetLiege.GetTitledFirstName]. The Ropsmann listen politely, as they always do. Then the eldest of the camp tells them, as the Ropsmann always have, that the spirits of the wood were here before the bear, and will be here after.
Perhaps it is time to listen to the bear.
The spirits of the wood were here first.

The stanitsa of [stanitsa_turned.GetName] has raised an altar to Ursun beside the old shrine. Nobody ordered it. The riders simply took up the faith of their comrades from the other stanitsas, and now the old shrine stands empty.
Ursun's people grow.

The mission to [stanitsa_mission.GetName] is ready to leave. The High Speaker's priests would bring Ursun to the stanitsa the Orthodoxy's way, with sermons, and with swords for anyone who will not listen. The druzhina of the Ice Court would do it another way, with titles for the headmen and good trade for the stanitsa.
The Orthodoxy's way: sermon and sword.
The Ice Court's way: titles and trade.

The mission has come back with nothing. The stanitsa heard the priests out, took the gifts, and then sent them away. The headmen are angry at being pushed, and the stanitsa will be hard to hold for some years.
They will come to Ursun in time.
The mission has done its work. The stanitsa has raised an altar to Ursun, and the headmen have sworn by the Father of Bears.
Ursun's people grow.

Ungol horsemen come out of the steppe at dawn and fall on one of the Ropsmann camps. They have done this for a thousand years, and for a thousand years the Ropsmann have answered the same way. The pikes are already coming out of the huts.
Form the pike wall. Let them ride onto it.
Into the woods. They cannot follow us there.
Give them some furs and let them go.

Gospodar merchants have come up the rivers to the Ropsmann camps, with salt, iron and vodka to trade for furs and amber. They are polite, and their prices are almost fair. The Erengrad market would pay more, but it is a long way to Erengrad.
Trade with them.
Take the amber to Erengrad ourselves.
Send them away. The camps are not a market.

All over Kislev the old peoples are becoming one. Gospodar, Ungol and Ropsmann marry each other, speak the same speech and call themselves Kislevites. In [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s camps the young people have begun to do the same. The elders ask what the Ropsmann are to be: Kislevites like everyone else, or Ropsmann still.
We are all Kislevites now.
We were here first. We stay Ropsmann.

An old man walks out of the woods with a staff and a bundle of birch-bark scrolls. He is a keeper of the tongue, one of the last who speak the old Ropsmann speech that Kislevarin grew from, and who know the songs of the first men of Kislev. He would teach them at [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s court, if anyone there wished to learn.
Stay, keeper. We wish to learn.
The old tongue belongs to the past.
Send a Mission to the Stanitsas
Send priests or druzhina to bring an Ungol or Ropsmann stanitsa of the northern gods to Ursun, Dazh and Tor. Ungols mostly listen. Ropsmann mostly do not.
Call the Ungol Rotas
Call the horse-archer rotas of the Ungol stanitsas to ride for you until the peace. Once in ten years.
Chosen by the Stanitsa
The stanitsa chose this character to lead it after their father.
Rotas Recently Called
The Ungol rotas rode for this character recently.
Mission Recently Sent
This character sent a mission to the stanitsas recently.
Fur and Amber Trade
Gospodar merchants trade for this character's furs and amber.
Ropsmann Ways
The Ropsmann here keep to their own tongue and ways, and hold out against the Kislevite melting pot.
Resents the Mission
The stanitsa sent the priests of Ursun away and is angry at being pushed.
Burned Camps
Raiders burned the camps here, and the people are rebuilding.
Raised me to the druzhina
Refused an Ungol the druzhina
Chosen over me
Came to Ursun
Ungol Horn Bow
A short recurved bow of horn and sinew, made for shooting from the saddle at a gallop. The stanitsa gave it to the son it chose to lead it.
Birch-Bark Chronicle
A bundle of birch-bark scrolls in the old Ropsmann tongue, holding the songs and laws of the first men of Kislev.
